questions.question: What happens if one drop of acid rain water is put on blue litmus paper?

options.text: Blue litmus paper will turn yellow.
No colour changes in litmus paper.
Blue litmus paper will turn red.
Blue litmus paper will turn black.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blue litmus paper will turn red**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acid rain** contains acids such as **sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄)** and **nitric acid (HNO₃)**, formed when sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) react with water vapor in the atmosphere.
 
• Blue litmus paper is an indicator used to test the **acidity** or **basicity** of a solution.
 
• When blue litmus paper comes in contact with an **acidic substance** (pH less than 7), it turns **red**, indicating the presence of an acid.
 
• Since acid rain water has a **low pH** (typically between 4-5), it is acidic in nature. Hence, when a drop of acid rain water is placed on blue litmus paper, the paper turns **red**.
 
• This reaction is due to the presence of **hydrogen ions (H⁺)** in the acid rain water, which interact with the litmus indicator, causing the color change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Litmus Paper:**

 
 
• Litmus paper is a **natural indicator** made from lichens. It is widely used to test the **acidity or alkalinity** of substances.
 
• Blue litmus paper turns **red** in the presence of an acid, while red litmus paper turns **blue** in the presence of a base.
 
• Neutral substances do not cause any color change in litmus paper.
 
 
 
• **Acid Rain:**
 
 
• Acid rain occurs due to the emission of **sulfur dioxide (SO₂)** and **nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)** from industrial processes, vehicular emissions, and burning of fossil fuels.
 
• These gases react with atmospheric water and oxygen to form **acids** such as sulfuric acid and nitric acid, which precipitate as acid rain.
 
• Acid rain has harmful effects on **plants, aquatic life, buildings**, and human health.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale:**
 
 
• The **pH scale** measures the acidity or alkalinity of a solution, ranging from **0 to 14**.
 
• A pH value **less than 7** indicates an acidic solution, while a value **greater than 7** indicates a basic solution.
 
• A pH of **7** indicates a **neutral** solution, such as pure water.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Acid Rain:**
 
 
• Acid rain damages crops, forests, and aquatic ecosystems by lowering the pH of soil and water bodies.
 
• It corrodes buildings, monuments, and infrastructure, especially those made of limestone or marble.
 
• Efforts to reduce acid rain include minimizing **SO₂ and NOₓ emissions** through cleaner energy sources and stricter regulations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Indicators:** Indicators like litmus paper, phenolphthalein, and methyl orange help in identifying the nature of substances (acidic, basic, or neutral).
 
• **Reducing Acid Rain:** Adoption of renewable energy sources, installation of scrubbers in industries, and promoting afforestation are effective measures to mitigate acid rain.
 
• **Global Efforts:** International agreements like the **Clean Air Act** and protocols aim to reduce emissions causing acid rain.

questions.question: In human female, when egg is not fertilised, which of the following process takes place?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Menstruation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Menstruation** refers to the periodic shedding of the uterine lining (endometrium) in human females when fertilization of the egg does not occur.
 
• This process is part of the **menstrual cycle**, which typically lasts around **28 days**, though it can range from 21 to 35 days in different individuals.
 
• Menstruation occurs due to a drop in the levels of the hormones **estrogen** and **progesterone**, leading to the breakdown and discharge of the endometrial lining.
 
• The **discharge** during menstruation consists of blood, mucus, and tissue from the uterine lining, and it typically lasts for **3-7 days**.
 
• It is a natural and essential part of the female reproductive cycle, preparing the body for a potential pregnancy each month. If fertilization does not occur, the uterine lining is shed, and the cycle begins again.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true according to the sign convention for spherical lenses?

options.text: Object height is negative when the object is placed above the principal axis.
The focal length of a convex lens is positive.
The focal length of a concave lens is negative.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Object height is negative when the object is placed above the principal axis.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** Object distance is negative.

 
 
• According to the standard sign convention for spherical lenses, distances measured against the direction of the incoming light are taken as negative. Since the object is usually placed to the left of the lens (against the direction of light), the object distance is always negative.
 
• *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** Object height is negative when the object is placed above the principal axis.
 
 
• In the sign convention for spherical lenses, heights measured above the principal axis are considered positive, while heights measured below are taken as negative. Thus, the object height cannot be negative if the object is placed above the principal axis.
 
• *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 3:** The focal length of a convex lens is positive.
 
 
• A convex lens converges light rays, and its focal point lies on the side opposite to the object. Therefore, the focal length of a convex lens is taken as positive.
 
• *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 
 
• **Statement 4:** The focal length of a concave lens is negative.
 
 
• A concave lens diverges light rays, and its focal point lies on the same side as the object. Therefore, the focal length of a concave lens is taken as negative.
 
• *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sign Convention for Spherical Lenses:**

 
 
• Distances are measured from the optical center of the lens.
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incoming light are positive, while distances against the direction of light are negative.
 
• Heights above the principal axis are positive, and heights below the axis are negative.
 
 
 
• **Convex Lens Characteristics:**
 
 
• A convex lens is a converging lens that focuses light rays to a point on the other side of the lens.
 
• Focal length is positive, and the lens is used in applications like magnifying glasses, cameras, and telescopes.
 
 
 
• **Concave Lens Characteristics:**
 
 
• A concave lens is a diverging lens that spreads out light rays, appearing to come from a focal point on the same side as the object.
 
• Focal length is negative, and the lens is used in applications like eyeglasses for myopia (short-sightedness) and peepholes.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Spherical Lenses:**
 
 
• Convex lenses are used in devices like projectors, microscopes, and cameras due to their converging properties.
 
• Concave lenses are used in optical instruments like binoculars and corrective glasses for certain vision impairments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lens Formula:**

 
 
• The lens formula is given by **1/f = 1/v - 1/u**, where:

 
 
• **f**: Focal length of the lens
 
• **v**: Image distance
 
• **u**: Object distance
 
 
 
• This formula applies to both convex and concave lenses, with the sign convention dictating the values of **v**, **u**, and **f**.
 
 
 
• **Magnification:**
 
 
• The magnification (M) of a lens is given by **M = h'/h = -v/u**, where:
 
 
• **h'**: Height of the image
 
• **h**: Height of the object
 
 
 
• A positive magnification indicates an erect image, while a negative magnification indicates an inverted image.

questions.question: Which of the following is a molecule of a compound?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**H₂O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **H₂O**, commonly known as water, is a **molecule of a compound**. It is composed of two hydrogen atoms covalently bonded to one oxygen atom.
 
• A **compound** is defined as a substance that consists of atoms of two or more different elements chemically bonded together in a fixed ratio. **H₂O** fits this definition as it contains hydrogen and oxygen atoms.
 
• Other options like **H₂, N₂, and O₂** are **molecules of elements**, not compounds, as they consist of only one type of element (hydrogen, nitrogen, or oxygen respectively).
 
• Water is an essential compound in nature, serving as a solvent in various biological and chemical processes. Its molecular structure contributes to its unique properties like high boiling and melting points, surface tension, and ability to dissolve many substances.
 
• **H₂O** is formed through chemical reactions such as the combination of hydrogen gas and oxygen gas in the presence of energy (e.g., combustion reaction).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **H₂:**

 
 
• **H₂** is a molecule of the element hydrogen. It consists of two hydrogen atoms bonded covalently.
 
• It is not a compound because it contains only one type of element.
 
• Hydrogen gas is commonly used in industries, such as in fuel cells and as a reducing agent in chemical reactions.
 
 
 
• **N₂:**
 
 
• **N₂** is a molecule of the element nitrogen. It is composed of two nitrogen atoms bonded by a triple covalent bond, making it highly stable.
 
• It is not a compound as it contains only one type of element.
 
• Nitrogen gas makes up about **78%** of Earth's atmosphere and is essential for life, especially in the nitrogen cycle.
 
 
 
• **O₂:**
 
 
• **O₂** is a molecule of the element oxygen, consisting of two oxygen atoms bonded by a double covalent bond.
 
• It is not a compound as it contains only oxygen atoms.
 
• Oxygen gas is crucial for respiration in most living organisms and is vital for combustion processes.
 
 
 
• **H₂O:**
 
 
• **H₂O** is a compound because it contains two different elements: hydrogen and oxygen.
 
• Its molecular shape is bent due to the lone pairs on the oxygen atom, resulting in a **polar molecule**.
 
• It exhibits unique properties like being a universal solvent, having high specific heat capacity, and supporting life on Earth.
 
• Examples of its use include drinking water, agriculture, and as a solvent in laboratories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Difference Between Molecules of Elements and Compounds:**

 
 
• A molecule of an element contains atoms of only one type of element (e.g., H₂, O₂, N₂).
 
• A molecule of a compound contains atoms of two or more different elements chemically bonded (e.g., H₂O, CO₂, NaCl).
 
 
 
• **Examples of Compounds:**
 
 
• **Water (H₂O):** Composed of hydrogen and oxygen.
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂):** Composed of carbon and oxygen.
 
• **Sodium Chloride (NaCl):** Composed of sodium and chlorine.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Water:**
 
 
• High boiling point (100°C) and freezing point (0°C) due to hydrogen bonding.
 
• Excellent solvent for ionic and polar substances.
 
• Essential for biological processes like photosynthesis and cellular respiration.

questions.question: The speed of sound (v) is calculated by multiplying which two wave properties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wavelength and Frequency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The speed of sound (v)** is calculated using the formula: **v = λ × f**, where **λ (wavelength)** is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs of a wave, and **f (frequency)** is the number of vibrations or oscillations per second.
 
• The **wavelength (λ)** is typically measured in meters (m), while the **frequency (f)** is measured in hertz (Hz). Multiplying these two properties gives the speed of sound in meters per second (m/s).
 
• **Sound waves** are longitudinal waves, meaning that the particles of the medium through which the sound travels oscillate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• The speed of sound depends on the properties of the medium, such as density and elasticity, but the relationship between wavelength and frequency remains constant for a given medium.
 
• The formula **v = λ × f** is fundamental in wave mechanics and applies to both sound and electromagnetic waves.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Amplitude and Frequency:** Amplitude refers to the maximum displacement of particles from their mean position in a wave, and frequency is the number of oscillations per second. While both are important wave properties, they do not determine the speed of sound. Instead, amplitude is related to the energy of the wave, and frequency is related to pitch.
 
• **Wavelength and Amplitude:** Wavelength is the distance between two consecutive points of similar phase (like crests), while amplitude determines the wave's intensity or loudness. Their product does not give the speed of sound.
 
• **Amplitude and Time Period:** Time period (T) is the reciprocal of frequency (T = 1/f). While both amplitude and time period are critical in describing wave behavior, their product does not relate to the speed of sound.
 
• **Physical Factors Affecting Sound Speed:** The speed of sound varies with the medium's properties, such as temperature, density, and elasticity. For example:
 
 
• In air at 20°C, the speed of sound is approximately **343 m/s**.
 
• In water, the speed of sound is significantly higher, around **1482 m/s**, due to the medium's higher density and elasticity.
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:**
 
 
• In sonar technology, the relationship between wavelength, frequency, and speed is used to detect objects underwater.
 
• In musical instruments, tuning is based on frequency, which affects the speed and wavelength of sound waves in air.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Frequency (f):** It is measured in hertz (Hz) and represents the number of wave cycles per second. For example, a sound wave with a frequency of 100 Hz completes 100 oscillations per second.
 
• **Wavelength (λ):** It is the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs of a wave, measured in meters (m). A longer wavelength corresponds to a lower frequency for a given speed of sound.
 
• **Relationship Between Speed, Wavelength, and Frequency:** For a wave propagating through a medium, the speed remains constant unless the medium’s properties change. Thus, if the wavelength increases, the frequency decreases proportionally, and vice versa.
 
• **Medium Dependency:** In gases, the speed of sound is slower compared to liquids and solids, as the intermolecular forces and density differ across these states of matter.

questions.question: A particle’s velocity-time graph is a straight line with a negative slope. What does this indicate about the particle’s motion?

options.text: The particle is speeding up in the positive direction.
The particle is slowing down if moving in the positive direction.
The particle is moving with increasing acceleration.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The particle is slowing down if moving in the positive direction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neurons**, also called nerve cells, are the fundamental units of the nervous system responsible for transmitting information throughout the body.
 
• A typical neuron consists of **four main components: dendrites, cell body (soma), axon, and nerve endings**.
 
• **Dendrites**__: These are branched projections that receive electrical signals from other neurons and convey them to the cell body.
 
• __**Cell Body (Soma)**__: This is the central part of the neuron, containing the nucleus and cytoplasm. It processes incoming signals and generates outgoing signals.
 
• __**Axon**__: A long, thread-like projection that transmits signals away from the cell body to other neurons, muscles, or glands.
 
• __**Nerve Endings (Axon Terminals)**__: These are the endpoints of the axon, where the neuron communicates with other cells via neurotransmitter release at synapses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Neurons:**

 
 
• **Sensory Neurons**: Transmit sensory information (e.g., touch, light, sound) from sensory receptors to the central nervous system (CNS).
 
• **Motor Neurons**: Send signals from the CNS to muscles or glands, enabling movement or secretion.
 
• **Interneurons**: Connect sensory and motor neurons within the CNS for processing and integration of information.
 
 
 
• **Function of Dendrites:** Dendrites increase the surface area of neurons for receiving signals and play a crucial role in integrating incoming information.
 
• **Structure of the Axon:** Axons are often covered by a **myelin sheath**, which is made up of glial cells. This sheath increases the speed of electrical signal transmission.
 
• **Synapse:** The junction between a nerve ending and another cell (e.g., neuron, muscle cell) where neurotransmitters facilitate communication.
 
• **Neurotransmitters:** Chemicals like dopamine, serotonin, and acetylcholine released at synapses to transmit signals between neurons.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Neuron Communication:** Neurons transmit signals via **electrical impulses (action potentials)** and chemical signals (neurotransmitters).
 
• **Myelination:** Myelin sheaths are formed by **Schwann cells** in the peripheral nervous system (PNS) and **oligodendrocytes** in the central nervous system (CNS).
 
• **Diseases Related to Neurons:** Disorders like **Alzheimer's disease**, **Parkinson's disease**, and multiple sclerosis involve damage to neurons or their connections.
 
• **Neuroplasticity:** The ability of neurons to adapt, reorganize, and form new connections in response to learning or injury.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a homologous series of organic compounds?

options.text: A series of compounds having the same general formula, similar chemical properties, and consecutive members differing by a -CH2- group
A series of compounds with different functional groups but the same molecular formula
A series of elements with similar physical properties
A series of compounds that all have branched chains

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**A series of compounds having the same general formula, similar chemical properties, and consecutive members differing by a -CH2- group.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Definition of Homologous Series:** A homologous series is a group of organic compounds that follow a particular pattern, having the **same general formula**, similar chemical properties, and a regular difference in their molecular structures by a **-CH2- group**.
 
• **Consecutive Members Differ by -CH2-:** Each member in the homologous series differs from the next by a **-CH2-** unit. For example, in the alkane series, methane (CH4) and ethane (C2H6) differ by one -CH2- group.
 
• **Similar Chemical Properties:** Compounds in a homologous series exhibit similar chemical behavior because they have the **same functional group**. For instance, all alcohols (R-OH) show similar reactivity due to the hydroxyl group.
 
• **Physical Properties Show Gradation:** The physical properties, such as boiling points, melting points, and density, show a **gradual change** as the molecular size increases.
 
• **Examples of Homologous Series:** Common examples include the alkane series (CnH2n+2), alkene series (CnH2n), and alcohol series (CnH2n+1OH).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Characteristics of Homologous Series:**

 
 
• **General Formula:** All members of a homologous series can be represented by a single general formula. For example, alkanes can be represented as CnH2n+2.
 
• **Functional Group:** The chemical properties of the members are dictated by the presence of a **functional group**, such as -OH in alcohols or -COOH in carboxylic acids.
 
• **Gradation in Physical Properties:** The gradual change in physical properties is due to the increasing molecular mass or size. For instance, boiling points increase in the alkane series as more -CH2- groups are added.
 
 
 
• **Option-wise Analysis:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** Correct. It accurately describes the characteristics of a homologous series.
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect. A homologous series cannot have different functional groups; this would lead to entirely different chemical properties.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect. This describes elements with similar physical properties, not a homologous series.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect. Homologous series can include both straight-chain and branched compounds, but the statement that all members have branched chains is not true.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Homologous Series:**
 
 
• **Alkanes:** Methane (CH4), ethane (C2H6), propane (C3H8).
 
• **Alkenes:** Ethene (C2H4), propene (C3H6), butene (C4H8).
 
• **Alcohols:** Methanol (CH3OH), ethanol (C2H5OH), propanol (C3H7OH).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Functional Group:** The functional group determines the chemical reactivity of the compounds in the series. For example, -OH in alcohols makes them soluble in water and reactive towards acids.
 
• **Applications:** Homologous series help in the systematic study of organic compounds, prediction of properties, and identification of unknown compounds.
 
• **Industrial Relevance:** Many homologous series, such as alkanes and alcohols, are crucial in industries, including fuels, pharmaceuticals, and polymers.
 
• **Nomenclature:** Compounds in a homologous series follow the IUPAC nomenclature system, ensuring uniform naming.

questions.question: Two wires, A and B, of the same material, have the same length, but the cross-sectional area of wire A is twice that of wire B. The ratio of their resistances R_A : R_B is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 : 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Resistance and its formula**: The resistance (*R*) of a wire is given by the formula: *R = ρ × (L / A)*, where:

 
 
• **ρ (rho)**: Resistivity of the material (same for both wires, as they are of the same material).
 
• **L**: Length of the wire (same for both wires).
 
• **A**: Cross-sectional area of the wire.
 
 
 
• **Given condition**: Wire A has twice the cross-sectional area of wire B. Let the cross-sectional area of wire B be **A**, then the cross-sectional area of wire A will be **2A**.
 
• **Relation between resistances**: Since *L* and *ρ* are the same for both wires, the resistance ratio depends only on their cross-sectional areas. Using the formula *R ∝ 1/A*:
 
 
• Resistance of wire A, *R_A = ρ × (L / 2A)*.
 
• Resistance of wire B, *R_B = ρ × (L / A)*.
 
• Taking the ratio, *R_A : R_B = (L / 2A) : (L / A) = 1 : 2*.
 
 
 
• **Final result**: The ratio of their resistances is **1 : 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors affecting resistance**: The resistance of a wire depends on:

 
 
• **Length (L)**: Resistance increases with an increase in length.
 
• **Cross-sectional area (A)**: Resistance decreases with an increase in area.
 
• **Material**: The resistivity (*ρ*) of the material determines how much resistance it offers.
 
• **Temperature**: For most materials, resistance increases with an increase in temperature.
 
 
 
• **Applications of resistance**:
 
 
• Resistors are used in electrical circuits to control the flow of current.
 
• High-resistance materials are used as heating elements in devices like toasters and electric heaters.
 
 
 
• **Understanding resistivity**:
 
 
• Resistivity (*ρ*) is a material property that quantifies how strongly a material opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• It is measured in **ohm-meters (Ω·m)**.
 
• Materials with low resistivity (like copper and silver) are good conductors, while materials with high resistivity (like rubber and glass) are insulators.
 
 
 
• **Practical implications**:
 
 
• Thicker wires (larger cross-sectional area) have lower resistance and are used in high-current applications.
 
• Longer wires have higher resistance, so they are avoided in designs where minimal energy loss is required.

questions.question: According to Newton’s second law of motion, what happens when an unbalanced force is applied to an object?

options.text: The object moves in a circular path
The object comes to rest immediately
The object’s momentum changes in the direction of the applied force

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The object’s momentum changes in the direction of the applied force.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Newton’s Second Law of Motion** states that the rate of change of momentum of an object is directly proportional to the unbalanced force applied to it and occurs in the direction of the force.
 
• **Momentum** is defined as the product of the mass and velocity of an object. It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• When an **unbalanced force** is applied to an object, it creates an acceleration according to the equation **F = ma** (Force = Mass × Acceleration). This acceleration causes a change in the object’s velocity, and since momentum depends on velocity, the momentum of the object also changes.
 
• The change in momentum occurs in the **direction of the applied force**, which is why the object’s momentum changes in that specific direction.
 
• The other options are incorrect because:
 
 
• The object does not necessarily move in a circular path unless the force is centripetal (Option 1).
 
• The object does not come to rest immediately unless the force is applied in the opposite direction and is strong enough to stop the motion (Option 2).
 
• The momentum cannot remain unchanged when an unbalanced force is applied, as per Newton’s Second Law (Option 3).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Newton's Laws of Motion:**

 
 
• **First Law:** States that an object will remain at rest or in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted upon by an external force (Law of Inertia).
 
• **Second Law:** Explains how the velocity of an object changes when it is subjected to an external force, mathematically expressed as **F = ma**.
 
• **Third Law:** States that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
 
 
 
• **Momentum:**
 
 
• It is a measure of the motion of an object and is calculated as **p = mv**, where **p** is momentum, **m** is mass, and **v** is velocity.
 
• Momentum is conserved in an isolated system where no external forces act.
 
 
 
• **Unbalanced Force:**
 
 
• An unbalanced force occurs when the forces acting on an object are not equal in magnitude and direction, causing the object to accelerate.
 
• Example: A car accelerating forward when the engine applies a forward force greater than the resistive forces (friction and air resistance).
 
 
 
• **Applications of Newton’s Second Law:**
 
 
• It is used in designing vehicles to ensure proper acceleration and braking systems.
 
• It helps in understanding the motion of celestial bodies under gravitational forces.
 
• Engineers use it to calculate the forces acting on structures and machines.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SI Unit:** The SI unit of momentum is **kg·m/s**, and force is measured in **Newtons (N)**.
 
• **Real-life Example:** In sports, such as cricket, a fielder reduces the impact of catching a fast-moving ball by moving their hands backward to increase the time of impact, thereby reducing the force.
 
• **Impulse:** The change in momentum of an object is known as **impulse**, which is equal to the product of force and the time duration of the force applied.
 
• **Rocket Propulsion:** Newton’s Second Law is key to explaining how rockets launch, as the expulsion of gas creates a force that changes the rocket’s momentum.

The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement A:** The large spaces between gas particles allow them to be easily squeezed into smaller volumes.

 
 
• This statement is **correct**. Gases have a unique property where their particles are widely spaced compared to solids and liquids. These large intermolecular spaces allow gases to be compressed easily under pressure.
 
• For example, gases like oxygen and nitrogen can be compressed into cylinders for medical or industrial purposes.
 
 
 
• **Statement B:** Gas particles have a high average kinetic energy.
 
 
• This statement is also **correct**. The kinetic energy of gas particles is directly proportional to the temperature of the gas (measured in Kelvin). As temperature increases, the particles move faster, indicating higher kinetic energy.
 
• The kinetic energy of gas particles is a fundamental concept in the kinetic molecular theory of gases.
 
 
 
• **Both A and B are correct:**
 
 
• Both statements align with the properties of gases. Statement A explains why gases are compressible, while statement B explains the relationship between temperature and particle motion in gases.
 
• These properties are crucial for understanding gas behavior in various applications, such as industrial gas storage, thermodynamics, and fluid dynamics.

__

• The theory describes the behavior of gas particles, assuming they are in constant random motion.
 
• The average kinetic energy of gas particles depends only on the temperature of the gas.
 
• Gases are assumed to have negligible intermolecular forces, and collisions between particles are perfectly elastic.
 
 
 
• **Compressibility of Gases:**
 
 
• Gases can be compressed due to the large spaces between their particles, as opposed to solids and liquids, where particles are closely packed.
 
• This property is utilized in various applications, such as compressed natural gas (CNG) and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) storage.
 
 
 
• **Relationship Between Temperature and Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• The kinetic energy of gas particles is proportional to the absolute temperature (Kelvin scale).
 
• For example, doubling the temperature of a gas doubles the average kinetic energy of its particles.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Gas Properties:**
 
 
• Compressibility is crucial for gas storage in industries and medical applications.
 
• The relationship between temperature and kinetic energy is used in thermodynamics and heat engines.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Boyle’s Law:** At constant temperature, the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume, which explains the compressibility of gases.
 
• **Charles’s Law:** At constant pressure, the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature, linking temperature and particle motion.
 
• **Real vs. Ideal Gases:** While the above properties apply to ideal gases, real gases deviate under high pressure and low temperature due to intermolecular forces.
 
• **Practical Uses:** Understanding gas behavior is essential in fields like meteorology, aviation, and chemical engineering.

questions.question: From the given alternatives, which method of asexual reproduction involves the formation of a new plant from the broken portion of the parent plant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fragmentation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Fragmentation** is a type of asexual reproduction in which a new organism develops from a **fragment or broken portion** of the parent organism.
 
• This process is commonly observed in certain plants and organisms such as algae, fungi, and some animals like sponges and flatworms.
 
• The broken fragment of the parent plant has the ability to regenerate and grow into a complete, independent organism under suitable environmental conditions.
 
• Fragmentation is different from other methods of asexual reproduction like binary fission and spore formation, as it specifically involves the physical splitting of the parent organism.
 
• Examples of plants that reproduce through fragmentation include **hydra, moss, and liverwort**. Certain algae, such as **Spirogyra**, also exhibit this form of reproduction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Spore Formation:**

 
 
• Spore formation is another type of asexual reproduction where organisms produce **spores** that can grow into new individuals.
 
• It is common in fungi, bacteria, and certain plants like ferns and mosses.
 
• Spores are microscopic structures that are resistant to harsh conditions and can remain dormant until favorable conditions arise.
 
 
 
• **Fertilization:**
 
 
• Fertilization is a process of **sexual reproduction** where the male and female gametes fuse to form a zygote.
 
• This process is not related to asexual reproduction and involves genetic mixing of two parents.
 
• Examples include reproduction in humans, animals, and flowering plants.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission:**
 
 
• Binary fission is a method of asexual reproduction in unicellular organisms like **bacteria and amoeba**.
 
• The parent organism splits into two identical daughter organisms, each inheriting the genetic material of the parent.
 
• This process is faster and commonly observed in prokaryotic organisms.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Fragmentation:**
 
 
• Fragmentation is widely utilized in **horticulture** and agriculture to propagate plants.
 
• It ensures **genetic uniformity**, which is useful for maintaining desired traits in crops or ornamental plants.
 
• This method is particularly beneficial for reproducing species that do not produce viable seeds.

questions.question: A particle has zero kinetic energy. What can be concluded about the particle's motion?

options.text: It is moving with high acceleration
It is moving with uniform velocity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It must be at rest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE)** of a particle is given by the formula: **KE = (1/2)mv²**, where **m** is the mass of the particle and **v** is its velocity. If kinetic energy is zero, the velocity must also be zero.
 
• A particle with zero velocity implies that it is **not in motion**. Hence, the particle must be **at rest**.
 
• **Momentum** of a particle is given by the formula: **p = mv**. Since velocity (v) is zero, the momentum of the particle is also zero.
 
• The particle cannot have **maximum momentum** (as suggested in Option 1) or any motion-related property like acceleration (as suggested in Option 2) because both require movement.
 
• If the particle is at rest, it cannot move with a **uniform velocity** (as suggested in Option 4) or any velocity other than zero.
 
• **Conclusion:** A particle with zero kinetic energy is necessarily at rest__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy (KE):**

 
 
• Kinetic energy is a type of **mechanical energy** associated with the motion of an object.
 
• It depends on two factors: the **mass** of the object and the **square of its velocity**. Hence, even a small velocity contributes significantly to the particle's kinetic energy.
 
• Units: The SI unit of kinetic energy is the **joule (J)**.
 
 
 
• **Momentum:**
 
 
• Momentum is a vector quantity defined as the product of an object's **mass** and **velocity**.
 
• If the velocity is zero, the momentum of the particle is also zero, irrespective of its mass.
 
• Units: The SI unit of momentum is **kilogram meter per second (kg·m/s)**.
 
 
 
• **Rest and Motion:**
 
 
• An object is said to be at **rest** when its position does not change with respect to a reference point over time.
 
• An object is in **motion** when its position changes with respect to a reference point over time.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• Kinetic energy plays a crucial role in various fields such as **transportation**, **sports**, and **mechanical systems**.
 
• Examples: Moving vehicles, flying aircraft, spinning turbines, and flowing rivers all possess kinetic energy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Relation Between Kinetic Energy and Momentum:**

 
 
• Kinetic energy and momentum are related by the equation: **KE = p² / 2m**, where **p** is momentum and **m** is mass.
 
• If kinetic energy is zero, momentum must also be zero.
 
 
 
• **Zero Kinetic Energy:**
 
 
• An object with zero kinetic energy cannot move until acted upon by an external force, as per **Newton's First Law of Motion**.
 
• It signifies the absence of motion in the reference frame being observed.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Energy:**
 
 
• In an isolated system, the total energy (potential + kinetic) remains constant. If kinetic energy is zero, the energy might be in another form, like **potential energy**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding the nucleus?

options.text: Nucleus plays a central role in cellular reproduction.

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The nucleus plays a central role in cellular reproduction:** The nucleus is responsible for regulating the cell cycle, mitosis, and meiosis. It contains genetic information essential for cell division, ensuring the accurate transmission of DNA to daughter cells. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **The nucleus contains chromosomes:** Chromosomes are thread-like structures made of DNA and proteins found within the nucleus. They carry genetic information required for cellular functions and reproduction. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **The nuclear membrane is a double-layered structure:** The nuclear envelope consists of two lipid bilayers—an inner membrane and an outer membrane. This structure separates the nucleus from the cytoplasm. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• **Nuclear membrane is a non-porous and rigid structure:** This is incorrect because the nuclear membrane is porous, allowing the exchange of materials like RNA and proteins between the nucleus and cytoplasm. The pores are part of the nuclear pore complex, which facilitates selective transport. The membrane is also flexible, adapting to changes during cell division. *Hence, this statement is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nuclear Membrane:**

 
 
• The nuclear membrane, also known as the nuclear envelope, is a double-layered structure that separates the nucleus from the cytoplasm.
 
• It contains **nuclear pores**, which are complexes facilitating selective transport of molecules like RNA and proteins.
 
• The nuclear envelope disassembles during cell division (mitosis) and reassembles afterward.
 
 
 
• **Chromosomes:**
 
 
• Chromosomes are composed of **DNA and histone proteins**, forming a structure called chromatin.
 
• In humans, there are **46 chromosomes (23 pairs)**, which include autosomes and sex chromosomes.
 
• They are essential for carrying genetic information and guiding protein synthesis through gene expression.
 
 
 
• **Role of Nucleus in Cellular Reproduction:**
 
 
• The nucleus orchestrates both mitosis (cell division for growth and repair) and meiosis (cell division for reproduction).
 
• It ensures the accurate replication and distribution of genetic material through processes like DNA replication and chromosome segregation.
 
 
 
• **Nuclear Pore Complex:**
 
 
• The nuclear pores are large protein complexes embedded within the nuclear envelope.
 
• They regulate the selective transport of molecules between the nucleus and the cytoplasm, allowing the exchange of RNA, ribosomal subunits, and proteins.
 
• These pores play a crucial role in maintaining nuclear-cytoplasmic communication.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Nuclear Membrane Dynamics:**

 
 
• The nuclear membrane breaks down during mitosis to allow chromosome segregation.
 
• It reforms after mitosis to encapsulate the genetic material within the daughter nuclei.
 
 
 
• **Nucleus as the Control Center:**
 
 
• The nucleus regulates gene expression by controlling transcription (RNA synthesis).
 
• It stores genetic material in the form of DNA, which directs all cellular activities.

A train of length 239 m takes 20 seconds to pass another train 161 m long coming from the opposite direction.

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed in opposite direction = (Sum of lengths) ÷ Time

Relative Speed = (239 + 161) ÷ 20 = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s

Convert m/s to km/hr: 20 × (18/5) = 72 km/hr

Speed of second train = Relative Speed − Speed of first train = 72 − 43 = 29 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 29 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 239 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 161 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 43 km/hr

Time taken to cross each other = 20 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = S₁ + S₂

Distance = Relative Speed × Time

Conversion: 1 m/s = 18/5 km/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9cf6a78b8b886535c6769aecb15e884de01cbc647e4113039bed0945e8674a0d.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the speed of the second train be S₂ km/hr.

⇒ Total distance to be covered = L₁ + L₂

⇒ Distance = 239 + 161 = 400 m

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = Total Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Relative Speed = 400 ÷ 20 = 20 m/s

⇒ Relative Speed in km/hr = 20 × (18/5)

⇒ Relative Speed = 4 × 18 = 72 km/hr

⇒ Since they are moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂

⇒ 72 = 43 + S₂

⇒ S₂ = 72 − 43

⇒ S₂ = 29 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 29 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S1 + S2). If they move in the same direction, it is the difference (S1 − S2).

Crossing Distance

To cross each other completely, the total distance covered is always the sum of the lengths of both trains (L1 + L2), regardless of direction.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

questions.question: When x is added to each of 10, 14, 38 and 28, then the numbers so obtained, in this order, are in proportion. Then, if 3x : y :: y : (5x - 6) , and y > 0 , what is the value of y ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For numbers a, b, c, d to be in proportion by adding x, x = (ad − bc) / ((b + c) − (a + d))

x = (10 × 28 − 14 × 38) / ((14 + 38) − (10 + 28)) = (280 − 532) / (52 − 38) = −252 / 14 = −18

Given 3x : y :: y : (5x − 6) ⇒ y² = 3x(5x − 6)

y² = 3(−18) × [5(−18) − 6] = −54 × (−90 − 6) = −54 × −96 = 5184

y = √5184 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given numbers: 10, 14, 38, 28

Condition: (10 + x), (14 + x), (38 + x), (28 + x) are in proportion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e605a4867c54902c885a2ca29502cb3dbf8c0f210acf4cac5aab87eb16025c1.png] 

From the proportion:

⇒ (10 + x) / (14 + x) = (38 + x) / (28 + x)

⇒ (10 + x)(28 + x) = (14 + x)(38 + x)

⇒ 280 + 10x + 28x + x² = 532 + 14x + 38x + x²

⇒ 280 + 38x = 532 + 52x

⇒ 52x − 38x = 280 − 532

⇒ 14x = −252

⇒ x = −18

Now, given 3x : y :: y : (5x − 6):

⇒ y² = 3x × (5x − 6)

⇒ y² = 3(−18) × [5(−18) − 6]

⇒ y² = −54 × (−90 − 6)

⇒ y² = −54 × −96

⇒ y² = 5184

⇒ y = √5184

⇒ y = 72 (Since y > 0)

**∴ The correct answer is 72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

If a, b, c are in continued proportion, then b is the mean proportional where b² = ac or b = √ac.

Fourth Proportional

If a, b, c, d are in proportion, then d is called the fourth proportional, and a/b = c/d or ad = bc.

Third Proportional

In the continued proportion a : b :: b : c, c is the third proportional to a and b, given by c = b² / a.

In a right-angled triangle, if the angle of elevation/depression is 45°, then the Perpendicular and Base are always equal (Ratio 1 : 1).

∴ Horizontal distance = 15 m

**∴ The correct answer is 15 m.**

**Given:**

Height of the building (AB) = 15 m

Angle of depression from top A to point C = 45°

Angle of elevation from point C to top A = 45° (Alternate interior angles)

questions.question: A class of 75 students took a Physics test. 22 students had an average score of 85. The other students had an average score of 95. What is the average score (rounded off to one decimal place) of the whole class?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the base average for all students is 95.

Group 1 (22 students) has an average of 85, which is 10 less than 95.

Total deviation = 22 × (−10) = −220.

Average deviation for the whole class = −220 ÷ 75 ≈ −2.93.

Whole class average = 95 − 2.93 = 92.066... ≈ 92.1.

**∴ The correct answer is 92.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Total students = 75 | Group 1 = 22 students | Average 1 = 85 | Average 2 = 95

Formula: Combined Average = (n₁ × x₁ + n₂ × x₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/79b868a44fed53313e3366ec7126be2adf92cc20948391b9c42896b9975aec51.png] ⇒ Number of students in Group 2 = 75 − 22 = 53 ⇒ Sum of scores for Group 1 = 22 × 85 = 1870 ⇒ Sum of scores for Group 2 = 53 × 95 = 5035 ⇒ Total sum of scores = 1870 + 5035 = 6905 ⇒ Combined Average = 6905 ÷ 75 ⇒ Combined Average = 92.0666... ⇒ Rounded Average ≈ 92.1

**∴ The correct answer is 92.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When groups have different sizes, the combined average is the sum of products of group sizes and their averages, divided by the total count.

Deviation Method

Assume a temporary mean to simplify calculations. The true mean = Assumed Mean + (Sum of deviations ÷ Total count).

Rounding Rule

To round to one decimal place, look at the second decimal digit; if it is 5 or more, increase the first decimal digit by 1.

questions.question:
The curved surface area and the volume of a cylindrical pipe is 565.2 m² and 1,695.6 m³ , respectively. Find the total surface area of the pipe.

(Use pi = 3.14 )
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Volume to CSA = (πr²h) / (2πrh) = r/2

⇒ r/2 = 1695.6 ÷ 565.2 = 3

⇒ Radius (r) = 6 m

⇒ TSA = CSA + 2 × π × r²

⇒ TSA = 565.2 + 2 × 3.14 × 36 = 565.2 + 226.08 = 791.28 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 791.28 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 565.2 m², Volume (V) = 1695.6 m³, π = 3.14

Formulae: Volume = πr²h | CSA = 2πrh | TSA = CSA + 2πr²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e017ef5be3ee58fc12c93be142b44f81c17ccc3b0706f592d2088cfe4456ec69.png] 

⇒ Volume / CSA = (πr²h) / (2πrh) = 1695.6 / 565.2

⇒ r / 2 = 3

⇒ r = 6 m

⇒ TSA = CSA + 2 × π × r²

⇒ TSA = 565.2 + 2 × 3.14 × (6)²

⇒ TSA = 565.2 + 6.28 × 36

⇒ TSA = 565.2 + 226.08

⇒ TSA = 791.28 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 791.28 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The sum of the area of the curved surface and the two circular bases: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r).

Volume and Radius Relationship

For any cylinder, the radius can be directly found if Volume (V) and Curved Surface Area (CSA) are known: r = 2V ÷ CSA.

Hollow Cylinder Volume

If the pipe has thickness, the volume of material is given by V = πh(R² − r²), where R is outer and r is inner radius.

questions.question: The monthly incomes of two friends, David and Ajay, are in the ratio 5 : 8, and each of them saves ₹72,000 every month. If the ratio of their monthly expenditure is 1 : 4, find the monthly income of David (in ₹).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cross Product Method:

Units difference = (5 × 4) − (8 × 1) = 20 − 8 = 12 units

Value difference = ₹72,000 × (4 − 1) = ₹2,16,000

12 units = ₹2,16,000 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹18,000

David's Income = 5 units × 18,000 = ₹90,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹90,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Income ratio (David : Ajay) = 5 : 8

Expenditure ratio (David : Ajay) = 1 : 4

Savings for each = ₹72,000

**Formula Used:**

Income − Savings = Expenditure

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f1ae8aa1201fd23521deed1116c68bdafefee0a3ca9c13b600382cb3a6e75d55.png] 

Let David's income be 5x and Ajay's income be 8x.

⇒ (5x − 72000) / (8x − 72000) = 1 / 4

⇒ 4 × (5x − 72000) = 1 × (8x − 72000)

⇒ 20x − 288000 = 8x − 72000

⇒ 20x − 8x = 288000 − 72000

⇒ 12x = 216000

⇒ x = 216000 ÷ 12 = 18000

⇒ David's monthly income = 5x = 5 × 18000 = 90000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹90,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Income, Expenditure & Savings Relation

The fundamental relation is Income = Expenditure + Savings. If savings are constant, the difference in income units corresponds to the difference in expenditure units after scaling.

Cross-Multiplication Method

For two ratios a:b and c:d where a fixed value k is added/subtracted: 1 unit = |(b×c − a×d)| / |k×(c − d)|.

Equating Ratio Differences

When savings are equal, ensure the difference between income and expenditure units is the same for both persons by multiplying the ratios with suitable constants.

questions.question: Given that C is the third proportional of 59 and B. If B is the sum of the first three even natural numbers, then find the value of C. (Round off the answer to two decimal places.)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

B = Sum of first three even natural numbers = 2 + 4 + 6 = 12.

Third Proportional C = B² ÷ First Term.

C = 12² ÷ 59 = 144 ÷ 59.

C ≈ 2.44.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: First term (a) = 59, Second term (b) = B.

B = First three even natural numbers (2, 4, 6).

Formula: If a, b, and C are in continued proportion, then a : b :: b : C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b64034b4c4fe1e38dba4f824e2abb3a866e3cf101fbceffe044c5e89616d6cd.png] 

⇒ B = 2 + 4 + 6 = 12

⇒ For third proportional: 59 ÷ 12 = 12 ÷ C

⇒ 59 × C = 12 × 12

⇒ C = 144 ÷ 59

⇒ C = 2.44067...

⇒ C ≈ 2.44 (rounded to two decimal places)

**∴ The correct answer is 2.44.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is given by √(a × b).

Fourth Proportional

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then the fourth proportional d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Sum of First n Even Numbers

The sum of the first n even natural numbers is calculated using the formula n × (n + 1).

Continued Proportion

If a, b, c are in continued proportion, then a/b = b/c, which implies b² = ac.

questions.question: One pipe can fill a tank in 11 minutes, while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 22 minutes. If both the pipes are opened together when the tank is empty, how many minutes will it take to fill one-half of the tank?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of filling pipe = 1/11 per minute.

Rate of emptying pipe = 1/22 per minute.

Net rate of both pipes = 1/11 − 1/22 = 1/22 per minute.

Time for full tank = 22 minutes.

Time for half tank = 22 ÷ 2 = 11 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Fill time = 11 min, Empty time = 22 min.

Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM of 11 and 22.

⇒ Total capacity = 22 units.

Combined efficiency of (A + B) = 2 − 1 = 1 unit/min.

⇒ Target to fill = 1/2 × Total Capacity

⇒ Work = 1/2 × 22 = 11 units.

⇒ Time required = Work ÷ Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time = 11 ÷ 1 = 11 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Negative Work Concept

In pipes and cisterns, a filling pipe has positive efficiency, while an outlet or emptying pipe has negative efficiency.

Total Work Formula

Time required = Total Work ÷ Net Efficiency. Total work is usually taken as the LCM of time taken by individual pipes.

Partial Filling

If only a fraction of the tank needs to be filled, multiply the total capacity by that fraction before dividing by efficiency.

questions.question: In quadrilateral PQRS, the bisectors of angle R and angle S meet at the point T (inside the quadrilateral) and angle STR = 42.5^circ . If the ratio of angle P to angle Q is 8 : 9, then what is the difference between the measures of angle Q and angle P ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Property: In quadrilateral PQRS, the angle between bisectors of ∠R and ∠S is ∠STR = (∠P + ∠Q) / 2.

∠P + ∠Q = 2 × 42.5° = 85°.

Ratio P : Q = 8 : 9, Sum of ratios = 8 + 9 = 17 units.

17 units = 85° → 1 unit = 5°.

Difference between ∠Q and ∠P = (9 − 8) units = 1 unit = 5°.

**∴ The correct answer is 5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠STR = 42.5°, Ratio ∠P : ∠Q = 8 : 9.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles of a triangle = 180°; Sum of angles of a quadrilateral = 360°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/82e0781d6ae5d1d067d0ec94b3b757ace7dc8568f494b7c7f2f780392982c6a1.png] 

⇒ In ΔSTR, ∠STR + ∠TSR + ∠TRS = 180°

⇒ 42.5° + ∠S/2 + ∠R/2 = 180°

⇒ (∠S + ∠R)/2 = 180° − 42.5° = 137.5°

⇒ ∠S + ∠R = 137.5° × 2 = 275°

⇒ In quadrilateral PQRS, ∠P + ∠Q + ∠R + ∠S = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q + 275° = 360°

⇒ ∠P + ∠Q = 85°

⇒ Let ∠P = 8x and ∠Q = 9x

⇒ 8x + 9x = 85° ⇒ 17x = 85° ⇒ x = 5°

⇒ Difference = ∠Q − ∠P = 9x − 8x = x = 5°

**∴ The correct answer is 5°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all interior angles of any quadrilateral is always 360°.

Adjacent Angle Bisectors

The angle formed by the bisectors of two adjacent angles of a quadrilateral is equal to half the sum of the other two angles: ∠T = (∠P + ∠Q)/2.

Opposite Angle Bisectors

The acute angle formed by the intersection of bisectors of two opposite angles is equal to half the difference of the other two angles.

questions.question: X people were given a contract for doing a piece of work in 36 days. 3 people did not turn up to work due to sickness, and the rest of the people completed the work in 39 days. What is the value of X?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time Ratio = 36 : 39 → 12 : 13

Since work is constant, Men Ratio is inverse of Time Ratio = 13 : 12

Difference in ratio parts = 13 − 12 = 1 unit

Given, 1 unit = 3 people

Value of X (Original Men) = 13 units = 13 × 3 = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Initial number of people = X

Initial time taken = 36 days

Number of people after 3 people didn't turn up = X − 3

Actual time taken = 39 days

Formula Used: M₁ × D₁ = M₂ × D₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d525f3ae523ab79221146cb2537bb7b355bab274f426425babbdfc248d5ed0dd.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ X × 36 = (X − 3) × 39

⇒ 36X = 39X − 117

⇒ 39X − 36X = 117

⇒ 3X = 117

⇒ X = 117 ÷ 3

⇒ X = 39

**∴ The correct answer is 39.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

For work problems involving men (M), days (D), and hours (H), the formula is (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂.

Inverse Proportion in Work

The number of people is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a constant amount of work (M ∝ 1/D).

Unitary Method for Time & Work

If one person can do a job in 'n' days, then their work rate is 1/n per day.

questions.question: The number of prime numbers lying between 309 and 320 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Numbers between 309 and 320 are 310, 311, 312, 313, 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 319.

Exclude evens (310, 312, 314, 316, 318) and multiples of 5 (315).

Check remaining: 311 (Prime), 313 (Prime), 317 (Prime), 319 (11 × 29).

Total prime numbers = 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Range of numbers between 309 and 320.

**Method Used:** Primality testing of numbers within the specified interval.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5a80a7c9d410ed2e0078b23cb6f6fe0ee0301a8bf6821eb7af02410710111977.png] 

⇒ Numbers to check: {310, 311, 312, 313, 314, 315, 316, 317, 318, 319}

⇒ For a number n to be prime, it must not be divisible by any prime number ≤ √n.

⇒ √320 ≈ 17.88. Check divisibility by 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17.

⇒ 311: Not div. by 2, 3 (sum=5), 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 → Prime

⇒ 313: Not div. by 2, 3 (sum=7), 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 → Prime

⇒ 315: Divisible by 5 (ends in 5) → Composite

⇒ 317: Not div. by 2, 3 (sum=11), 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 → Prime

⇒ 319: Divisible by 11 (3 − 1 + 9 = 11) → Composite (11 × 29)

⇒ Total Primes = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Prime Number Definition

A natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself.

Primality Test

To check if N is prime, test its divisibility by all prime numbers up to √N.

Divisibility Rule for 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and the sum of digits at even positions is 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: The average age of 43 students of a class is 13 years. If the age of the teacher is also included, the average age of the whole group becomes 14 years. The age (in years) of the teacher is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Teacher’s age = New Average + (Initial number of students × Increase in average)

Increase in average = 14 − 13 = 1 year

Teacher’s age = 14 + (43 × 1)

Teacher’s age = 14 + 43 = 57 years

**∴ The correct answer is 57.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of students = 43 | Initial Average = 13 years | New Average (with teacher) = 14 years

**Formula Used:**

Total Age = Average × Number of People

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8bd2e09dff3bdf56b022d00bdd514792a4a4ec9ed075a8de83246a1093e71143.png] 

⇒ Total age of 43 students = 43 × 13

⇒ Total age of 43 students = 559 years

⇒ Total people including teacher = 43 + 1 = 44

⇒ Total age of 44 people = 44 × 14

⇒ Total age of 44 people = 616 years

⇒ Age of teacher = Total age of group − Total age of students

⇒ Age of teacher = 616 − 559 = 57 years

**∴ The correct answer is 57.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations).

Inclusion Shortcut

When one person joins and average increases: New person age = Old Average + [New total members × Increase in Avg].

Exclusion Shortcut

When one person leaves and average changes: Age of person who left = Old Average ± [New total members × Change in Avg].

Weighted Average

Combined Average = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is count and A is average.

questions.question:
Simplify the following.

 (a³ - b³)/(a² + ab + b²) + (a³ + b³)/(a² - ab + b²)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using algebraic identities, identify the standard reduction forms.

(a³ − b³) / (a² + ab + b²) = a − b

(a³ + b³) / (a² − ab + b²) = a + b

The expression simplifies to: (a − b) + (a + b) = 2a

**∴ The correct answer is 2a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: [(a³ − b³) / (a² + ab + b²)] + [(a³ + b³) / (a² − ab + b²)]

**Formula Used:**

1. a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

2. a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

**Calculation:**

⇒ [(a − b)(a² + ab + b²) / (a² + ab + b²)] + [(a + b)(a² − ab + b²) / (a² − ab + b²)]

⇒ (a − b) + (a + b)

⇒ a − b + a + b

⇒ 2a

**∴ The correct answer is 2a.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Identity

The sum of cubes can be factored as a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²).

Difference of Cubes Identity

The difference of cubes can be factored as a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).

Difference of Squares

One of the most used identities is a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b).

BODMAS rule

Always solve expressions in the order: Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication, and Addition/Subtraction.

questions.question: The income of Raman is ₹43,800. He saves 20% of his income. If his income increases by 36% and expenditure increases by 40%, then his savings will:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let initial Income = 100, then Savings = 20 and Expenditure = 80.

Change in Income (ΔI) = 100 × 36% = 36 units.

Change in Expenditure (ΔE) = 80 × 40% = 32 units.

Change in Savings (ΔS) = ΔI − ΔE = 36 − 32 = 4 units.

Value of 100 units = ₹43,800 ⇒ Value of 1 unit = ₹438.

Savings increase = 4 units × ₹438 = ₹1,752.

**∴ The correct answer is increase by ₹1,752.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Initial Income = ₹43,800 | Savings % = 20% | Income increase = 36% | Expenditure increase = 40%

Formula: Income = Expenditure + Savings

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/998919d9cab8360b6df28a4b610efef4ef1c4fddf8f06254739269d5ea274eab.png] 

⇒ Initial Savings = 20% of 43,800 = 0.20 × 43,800 = ₹8,760

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 43,800 − 8,760 = ₹35,040

⇒ Increase in Income = 36% of 43,800 = 0.36 × 43,800 = ₹15,768

⇒ Increase in Expenditure = 40% of 35,040 = 0.40 × 35,040 = ₹14,016

⇒ Change in Savings = Increase in Income − Increase in Expenditure

⇒ Change in Savings = 15,768 − 14,016 = ₹1,752

⇒ Since the result is positive, savings increase by ₹1,752.

questions.question: 3 cups and 4 glasses cost ₹270. If 2 more glasses are purchased, then the total amount becomes ₹330. Find the cost of a cup.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Extra cost for 2 more glasses = 330 − 270 = ₹60.

Cost of 1 glass = 60 ÷ 2 = ₹30.

Cost of 4 glasses = 4 × 30 = ₹120.

Cost of 3 cups = 270 − 120 = ₹150.

Cost of 1 cup = 150 ÷ 3 = ₹50.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

3 cups + 4 glasses = ₹270

3 cups + 6 glasses = ₹330

Method of Elimination for Linear Equations in two variables.

⇒ 3C + 6G = 330 → (2)

⇒ Subtracting equation (1) from equation (2):

⇒ (3C + 6G) − (3C + 4G) = 330 − 270

⇒ 2G = 60

⇒ G = 60 ÷ 2 = 30

⇒ Substituting G = 30 in equation (1):

⇒ 3C + 4 × 30 = 270

⇒ 3C + 120 = 270

⇒ 3C = 270 − 120

⇒ 3C = 150

⇒ C = 150 ÷ 3 = 50

**∴ The correct answer is ₹50.**

questions.question: In 2025, which authority raised serious objections to the Aparajita Bill 2024, calling its proposed punishments under BNS excessively harsh and disproportionate?

The correct answer is __**Central Government**__.

__
 
• The **Central Government** of India, primarily through the **Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**, raised serious objections in early **2025** regarding the **Aparajita Woman and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024**.
 
• The **Aparajita Bill** was passed by the **West Bengal Legislative Assembly** on **September 3, 2024**, in the aftermath of the **RG Kar Medical College** incident to strengthen laws against sexual violence.
 
• The **Central Government** argued that the proposed punishments under the bill were **excessively harsh and disproportionate** compared to the provisions laid out in the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, which replaced the Indian Penal Code. ***Hence, the statement is correct.***
 
• A major point of contention was the bill's provision for a **mandatory death penalty** in cases of rape where the victim dies or is left in a vegetative state, which the **Central Government** noted deviates from the discretionary power given to judges under the **BNS 2023**.
 
• The **Central Government** emphasized that since "Criminal Law" falls under the **Concurrent List** of the **Seventh Schedule** of the **Constitution of India**, any state amendment that is repugnant to a Central law requires **Presidential assent** under **Article 254(2)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Aparajita Bill, 2024:**
 
 
• The bill officially titled the **Aparajita Woman and Child (West Bengal Criminal Laws Amendment) Bill, 2024**, seeks to amend the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)**, **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)**, and the **POCSO Act** in their application to **West Bengal**.
 
• Key features include a **10-day investigation limit** for rape cases from the date of the preliminary report and the creation of a specialized **Aparajita Task Force** at the district level.
 
• The bill proposes **rigorous imprisonment** for life for the remainder of the convict's natural life without parole for various categories of sexual assault.
 
 
 
• **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS):**
 
 
• The **BNS** is the official criminal code of India, which came into effect on **July 1, 2024**, replacing the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** of **1860**.
 
• It contains **358 sections** and introduces new offenses like **terrorism**, **organized crime**, and **mob lynching**, while enhancing punishments for crimes against women and children.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Constitutional Repugnancy:** Under **Article 254**, if any provision of a law made by the Legislature of a State is **repugnant** to any provision of a law made by Parliament, the Central law prevails unless the State law has received the **assent of the President**.
 
• **Procedural Hurdles:** The **West Bengal Governor** referred the **Aparajita Bill** to the **President of India** for consideration, leading to the **Ministry of Home Affairs** scrutinizing it for legal and procedural consistency with existing national frameworks.
 
• **Legal Criticism:** Legal experts have noted that **mandatory capital punishment** has been previously struck down by the **Supreme Court** in cases like **Mithu vs. State of Punjab (1983)**, as it violates **Articles 14 and 21** of the Constitution by removing judicial discretion.
</ul
